page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2-standard-8 demonstrates moderate performance across a variety of workloads. Its multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, and its single-core Geekbench scores fall within the average tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 413.79 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, certain multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tasks, perform in the lower tier, indicating potential bottlenecks during highly parallelized, compute-intensive execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a balanced hardware profile suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.9 GB/sec, Redis database operations, and software compilation. It can also handle lightweight machine learning tasks, such as text generation with small models, though it is less optimal for heavy prompt processing or complex physics simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor at 2.8 GHz. It provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for most operations, including static web serving at 6.9 GB/sec, software compilation, and Redis database operations, though it exhibits weaker performance in highly parallelized multi-core tasks and physics simulations. Qualitatively, it offers a balanced resource profile for standard workloads, making it a cost-efficient option for general-purpose applications, web serving, and moderate database tasks.
